item.title: Vanessa Williams Says Two Music Legends Passed on ‘Save the Best for Last’ Before It Came Her Way: ‘I Was Third One Up’
item.description:
Here's a short and engaging podcast script based on the article:
[Upbeat music fades out, and the host begins speaking]
Host: "Welcome back to 'Music Moments'! Today, we're shining the spotlight on the talented Vanessa Williams. You might know her from her hit song 'Save the Best for Last', but did you know that she wasn't the first choice to record it?"
[Short music transition]
Host: "In a recent interview, Vanessa revealed that the song was actually offered to Bette Midler and Barbra Streisand before it landed on her lap. Can you imagine anyone else singing that iconic ballad? Williams was the third artist to be offered the song, and we're so glad she said yes!"
[Short music transition]
Host: "The song went on to become her highest-charting Billboard Hot 100 hit, spending five weeks at number one and earning two Grammy nominations. It's still one of her signature songs to this day. But Vanessa also shared that she had her eye on another big hit back in the day - Amy Grant's 'Baby Baby'. She wished she could have recorded that one, but it wasn't meant to be."
[Short music transition]
Host: "Vanessa Williams' music career is full of hits, from 'The Comfort Zone' to 'Colors of the Wind' from Disney's Pocahontas. And let's not forget her impressive acting career, with roles in Desperate Housewives, Ugly Betty, and more. She's a true talent, and we're so grateful for her music."
[Upbeat music starts playing again]
Host: "That's all for today's 'Music Moments'. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next one!"
